links.note: Explaining continent, ocean and island together - this concept is where the three are set against each other, islands being defined by what the continents leave out and continents excluded from the term only because they are so large. Already linked and defensible, so left alone.
The largest water bodies we see on the globe being called oceans - this concept's closing sentence. Already linked and correct.
A continent defined as a large continuous expanse of land, against a landmass as a large body of land - this concept sets the two terms against each other.
The Indian Ocean as the third largest, bounded by Asia to the north, Africa to the west and Australia to the east - this concept gives both the size order and those limits.
Flora as plant life - this concept is where marine flora, the algae and seaweeds, is set against marine fauna, the fish, dolphins and whales.
The Arabian Sea to the west and the Bay of Bengal to the east as the two parts of the Indian Ocean on either side of India - this concept's box. Already linked and correct.
A tsunami as a huge and powerful wave generally caused by an earthquake or volcanic eruption at the bottom of the ocean - this concept's definition. Already linked and correct.
The tsunami of 26 December 2004 that struck India and 13 other countries around the Indian Ocean - this concept's case. Already linked and correct.

Early warning systems, including the Indian Ocean Tsunami Warning System - this concept explains that tsunamis can often be detected before they hit a coast, which is why countries collaborate on them. Already linked and correct.
Continents countable in several ways, giving any number between four and seven depending on the criterion applied - this concept's argument. Already linked and correct.
Comparing North America with South America by size - this concept's diagram of relative sizes and its LET'S EXPLORE, which asks the reader to count squares and decide which of the two is larger.
Greenland as the largest island in the world, needing the ten largest Indian states added together to match it - this concept's detail. Already linked and correct.
India's two major island groups, the Andaman and Nicobar Islands in the Bay of Bengal and the Lakshadweep Islands in the Arabian Sea - this concept names both.
Dakshin Gangotri, India's first scientific base station in Antarctica, established in 1983 - this concept's account. Already linked and correct.
The United Nations designating 8 June as World Oceans Day - this concept's closing sentence.
Almost three-fourths of the Earth's surface covered with water, which is why it appears blue from space - this concept's statement. Already linked and correct.

Ranking the oceans and placing the Indian Ocean - this concept gives the order from Pacific down to Arctic and fixes the Indian Ocean by its limits, which is what makes entirely in the Southern Hemisphere the false pair.
Antarctica, mostly ice, as the site of Dakshin Gangotri and the Indian Antarctica Programme - this concept's section. Already linked and correct.
The lines dividing the oceans being no more than conventions, since seawater constantly flows across them - this concept's qualification of its own list. Already linked and correct.
Early astronauts lovingly calling the Earth the blue planet because most of its surface is covered with water - this concept's opening.
